title: Squared bar chart sheet
subject: Science
unit: Spring 2: Skeletons, muscles, nutrition and plants (Tribal Tales)
source: Seeded from science/y3 lesson 23 (Squared bar chart sheet (portal worksheet, printable or on a drawing tablet))
intro: Lesson 23: Cress results: graphs and conclusions. To understand how a bar chart helps us compare results and reach a conclusion

blocks.text: Label both axes, choose a scale, and draw the bars with a ruler, with gaps between them.

questions.q: Which pot did not grow at all, and why?
questions.a: Pot 3, because it had no water
questions.model: Find the 0 on the chart: pot 3. What was missing? Water. So pot 3 did not grow because seeds need water.

questions.q: Which pot grew slowly? What does that show?
questions.a: Pot 4 in the fridge; plants need warmth to grow well

questions.q: Is the tallest plant always the healthiest?
questions.a: No: pot 2 was tall but pale and weak

questions.q: Draw a bar chart of your own cress heights (or the example data) on the squared sheet.
questions.a: Four bars correctly labelled with heights in mm
questions.model: Teacher draws pot 1's bar on camera: find 40 on the side, draw the bar up to 40, label it 'Pot 1'.

questions.q: Write a conclusion of two sentences using 'because'.
questions.a: For example: Plants need water because pot 3 did not grow. Plants need light to be green because pot 2 was pale.

questions.q: If we did the test again, what would you change to make it better?
questions.a: For example: more pots of each kind, measure on the same days, use the same seeds.

questions.q: Bars on a bar chart show...
Big question: what do plants need?
questions.a: Light, water and warmth (and air and nutrients) to grow well.
